## Purpose

This procedure describes the extraction and colorimetric determination
of plant-available (extractable) phosphorus in soils. Two extraction
methods are presented: the Olsen method (0.5 M NaHCO~3~ at pH 8.5) for
neutral to alkaline soils, and the Bray-1 method (0.03 M NH~4~F +
0.025 M HCl) for acidic soils [@olsen1954; @bray1945]. Extractable P
is quantified colorimetrically using the ascorbic acid/molybdate blue
method [@murphy1962; @kuo1996].

Soil phosphorus availability is a key factor controlling plant
productivity, and excess P in runoff is a primary driver of
eutrophication in freshwater systems. Routine soil P testing guides
fertilizer management and helps assess the environmental risk of P loss
from agricultural and urban soils [@sharpley2003].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved (less than 2 mm) mineral soils from
  all EA Program field sites. The Olsen method is the default for
  southern California soils, which are typically neutral to alkaline.
  Use Bray-1 for soils with pH below 6.5.
- **Does not apply to:** Total phosphorus determination (requires acid
  digestion); dissolved reactive phosphorus in water samples (see
  [SOP-L303 Hach Colorimetric](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)); organic
  phosphorus fractionation
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Prepare and standardize reagents, maintain spectrophotometer |
| Trained Personnel | Perform extractions and analyses, report results |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |

## Definitions

- **Available phosphorus:** Phosphorus in soil solution and loosely sorbed fractions that can be taken up by plant roots; estimated by extraction with reagents that mimic root chemistry (Olsen bicarbonate in alkaline soils; Mehlich-3 or Bray in acid soils).
- **Bray P1 extraction:** An extraction using 0.025 M HCl + 0.03 M NH~4~F; removes acid-soluble (Al- and Fe-bound) phosphorus; appropriate for acid and neutral soils (pH < 7.4) but not for calcareous soils.
- **Mehlich-3 extraction:** A multi-element extractant (0.2 M CH~3~COOH + 0.25 M NH~4~NO~3~ + 0.015 M NH~4~F + 0.013 M HNO~3~ + 0.001 M EDTA); extracts plant-available P, K, Ca, Mg, and several micronutrients simultaneously; widely used in the eastern US and California.
- **Murphy-Riley method:** The standard colorimetric procedure for measuring dissolved reactive phosphorus; reacts phosphate with ammonium molybdate and ascorbic acid to form a blue phosphomolybdenum complex measured at 880 nm [@murphy1962].
- **Olsen extraction:** An extraction using 0.5 M NaHCO~3~ (pH 8.5); removes Ca-phosphate forms; the standard method for calcareous and alkaline soils (pH > 7.0); results expressed as mg P kg^-1^.
- **Sorption:** The attachment of phosphate ions to soil mineral surfaces (primarily Fe and Al oxides in acid soils; CaCO~3~ in alkaline soils); limits plant availability and affects the choice of extraction method.

## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Ascorbic acid, ammonium molybdate, and antimony
  potassium tartrate are mild irritants. Sulfuric acid (used in the
  color reagent) is corrosive at concentrated strengths. Ammonium
  fluoride (NH~4~F, Bray-1 extractant) is toxic and corrosive; handle
  in the fume hood. Sodium hydroxide (NaOH, for pH adjustment of Olsen
  reagent) is corrosive.
- **Physical:** Standard glassware handling risks.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (splash goggles when handling H~2~SO~4~ or NH~4~F)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Work in fume hood when handling NH~4~F

### Emergency Procedures

For acid or NH~4~F splashes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes.
For NH~4~F skin contact, flush with water and apply 2.5% calcium
gluconate gel if available. Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Reciprocating or end-over-end shaker | For extraction               |
| Spectrophotometer or colorimeter | 880 nm wavelength; Hach DR3900 ([SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)) or equivalent |
| Analytical balance (0.01 g)   | See [SOP-L102](SOP-L102-using-balances.qmd) |
| pH meter                      | For verifying extractant pH; see [SOP-L300](SOP-L300-pH-conductivity-bench.qmd) |
| Centrifuge or vacuum filtration apparatus | For clarifying extracts |
| Volumetric flasks (100 mL, 500 mL, 1 L) | Class A                  |
| Erlenmeyer flasks (125 or 250 mL) | One per sample plus blanks      |
| Graduated cylinders (25, 50, 100 mL) | For measuring extractant volumes |
| Pipettes (1--10 mL)          | Class A volumetric or calibrated micropipettes |
| Cuvettes (1 cm path length)  | Glass or polystyrene, matched               |
| Filter funnels and Whatman No. 42 filter paper | For clarifying extracts |

### Reagents -- Olsen Extraction

| Reagent                       | Preparation / Notes                       |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO~3~), 0.5 M at pH 8.5 | Dissolve 42.0 g NaHCO~3~ in approximately 900 mL DI water. Adjust to pH 8.5 with 1 M NaOH. Bring to 1 L. Prepare fresh weekly. |
| Activated charcoal (P-free)   | For decolorizing extracts; wash with 0.5 M NaHCO~3~ before use to remove any residual P [@olsen1954] |

### Reagents -- Bray-1 Extraction

| Reagent                       | Preparation / Notes                       |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Bray-1 extractant (0.03 M NH~4~F + 0.025 M HCl) | Dissolve 1.11 g NH~4~F in approximately 900 mL DI water. Add 2.1 mL concentrated HCl (12 M). Bring to 1 L. Prepare in fume hood. Store in polyethylene. [@bray1945] |

### Reagents -- Ascorbic Acid Colorimetric Determination

| Reagent                       | Preparation / Notes                       |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Sulfuric acid (H~2~SO~4~), 5 N | Dilute 70 mL concentrated H~2~SO~4~ (18 M) into approximately 400 mL DI water; bring to 500 mL after cooling. **Add acid to water.** |
| Ammonium molybdate ((NH~4~)~6~Mo~7~O~24~-4H~2~O), 4% | Dissolve 20 g in 500 mL DI water |
| Antimony potassium tartrate (K(SbO)C~4~H~4~O~6~-1/2H~2~O), 0.274% | Dissolve 0.274 g in 100 mL DI water |
| Ascorbic acid, 1.76% | Dissolve 1.76 g in 100 mL DI water. Prepare fresh daily. |
| **Combined color reagent** | Mix in order: 50 mL 5 N H~2~SO~4~ + 15 mL ammonium molybdate + 5 mL antimony potassium tartrate + 30 mL ascorbic acid. Prepare fresh for each batch. [@murphy1962] |
| Phosphorus stock standard (1000 mg/L P) | Dissolve 4.394 g anhydrous KH~2~PO~4~ (dried at 105 C) in 1 L DI water. Stable for months at 4 C. |
| Phosphorus working standards | Dilute stock to 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0 mg/L P in the appropriate extractant matrix (NaHCO~3~ or Bray-1) |

### Reagents -- General

| Reagent                       | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Deionized water (Type I or II) | From [*SOP-L11*](SOP-L11-milli-q-water.qmd) |


## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1. Air-dry the soil at room temperature until constant mass
2. Pass through a 2 mm sieve per
   [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)
3. Determine gravimetric moisture content on a subsample per
   [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd) to express results on a
   dry-weight basis

### Selecting the Extraction Method

| Soil pH    | Recommended Extractant | Reference             |
|:-----------|:-----------------------|:----------------------|
| 6.5 or above | Olsen (0.5 M NaHCO~3~, pH 8.5) | @olsen1954   |
| Below 6.5  | Bray-1 (0.03 M NH~4~F + 0.025 M HCl) | @bray1945 |

Determine soil pH per [SOP-L402](SOP-L402-soil-pH-salinity.qmd) before
selecting the extractant. If comparing across sites with widely varying
pH, consider using Mehlich-3 for all samples (consult the PI).

::: {.callout-note}
The Olsen extractant (NaHCO~3~ at pH 8.5) dissolves calcium phosphate
precipitates and reduces Fe^3+^ and Al^3+^ activity, releasing
adsorbed P. It works across a wide pH range but is the standard for
calcareous and alkaline soils. The Bray-1 extractant dissolves
Al-bound and Fe-bound P via fluoride complexation and acid dissolution;
it underestimates P in calcareous soils because the acid is neutralized
by free CaCO~3~ [@kuo1996].
:::

### Olsen Extraction

1. Weigh 2.50 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a 125 mL Erlenmeyer
   flask
2. Add approximately 0.25 g of P-free activated charcoal (pre-washed
   with 0.5 M NaHCO~3~)
3. Add 50 mL of 0.5 M NaHCO~3~ extractant (pH 8.5)
4. Stopper and shake on the reciprocating shaker at 180 oscillations
   per minute for 30 minutes
5. Filter immediately through Whatman No. 42 filter paper into a clean
   flask or tube. The filtrate should be clear and colorless; if
   yellow-brown, the charcoal was insufficient or not pre-washed.
6. Proceed to colorimetric analysis (Section 6.5) within 24 hours.
   Store extracts at 4 C if analysis is delayed.

### Bray-1 Extraction

1. Weigh 2.00 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a 125 mL Erlenmeyer
   flask
2. Add 20 mL of Bray-1 extractant (1:10 soil-to-solution ratio)
3. Shake on the reciprocating shaker at 180 oscillations per minute for
   5 minutes (the short extraction time is critical; extended shaking
   can re-adsorb released P)
4. Filter immediately through Whatman No. 42 filter paper
5. Proceed to colorimetric analysis (Section 6.5) within 24 hours

::: {.callout-important}
The Bray-1 extraction is exactly 5 minutes. Timing begins when the
extractant contacts the soil. Over-extraction will underestimate
available P due to re-sorption, while under-extraction will miss
slowly dissolving forms.
:::

### Colorimetric Determination (Ascorbic Acid/Molybdate Blue)

This procedure follows @murphy1962 as adapted by @kuo1996.

1. Prepare the combined color reagent fresh (see Section 5, Reagents)
2. Pipette a 5 mL aliquot of the filtered extract into a clean test
   tube or cuvette
3. For Olsen extracts: acidify the aliquot with 1 drop (approximately
   0.05 mL) of concentrated H~2~SO~4~ and swirl to expel CO~2~
   (the NaHCO~3~ matrix effervesces; wait until bubbling stops before
   adding color reagent)
4. Add 0.8 mL of the combined color reagent to each tube
5. Mix by vortexing or inversion
6. Allow the color to develop for 15 minutes at room temperature. The
   solution turns blue in proportion to the phosphorus concentration.
7. Read the absorbance at 880 nm (or 882 nm) against a DI water blank
   within 30 minutes of color development
8. Determine the P concentration from the calibration curve (Section
   6.6)

**Alternative: Hach DR3900 PhosVer 3 method.** If using the Hach
spectrophotometer, follow the PhosVer 3 (ascorbic acid) method per
[SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd), Program 490. Prepare
standards in the same extractant matrix as the samples.

### Calibration

1. Prepare a minimum of five working standards (e.g., 0, 0.1, 0.5,
   1.0, 2.0, 5.0 mg/L P) by diluting the stock standard with the
   same extractant used for the samples
2. Treat each standard exactly as the samples (acidification for Olsen,
   color reagent addition, timing)
3. Read absorbance at 880 nm
4. Plot absorbance versus concentration and fit a linear regression.
   Acceptable $r^2$ is 0.995 or higher.

### Calculations

**Extractable P in soil (mg P / kg dry soil):**

$$
P_{\text{soil}} = \frac{C \times V}{M \times \left(\frac{100}{100 + \theta_H}\right)}
$$

where $C$ = P concentration in the extract (mg/L), $V$ = volume of
extractant (mL), $M$ = mass of air-dried soil (g), and $\theta_H$ =
hygroscopic moisture (%, determined per
[SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)). The term
$\frac{100}{100 + \theta_H}$ converts the air-dried mass to an
oven-dry basis.

For the Olsen method with the standard parameters (2.50 g soil, 50 mL
extractant):

$$
P_{\text{soil}} \; (\text{mg/kg}) = C \times \frac{50}{2.50} \times \frac{100 + \theta_H}{100} = C \times 20 \times \frac{100 + \theta_H}{100}
$$

For Bray-1 (2.00 g soil, 20 mL extractant):

$$
P_{\text{soil}} \; (\text{mg/kg}) = C \times \frac{20}{2.00} \times \frac{100 + \theta_H}{100} = C \times 10 \times \frac{100 + \theta_H}{100}
$$


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Interpretation of Olsen P

| Olsen P (mg/kg) | Classification | Agronomic Interpretation               |
|:-----------------|:---------------|:---------------------------------------|
| Less than 5      | Very low       | P deficiency likely; fertilize         |
| 5 -- 10          | Low            | P may limit yield; fertilize           |
| 10 -- 20         | Medium         | Adequate for most crops                |
| 20 -- 40         | High           | No response to added P expected        |
| Greater than 40  | Very high      | Excess P; environmental risk of runoff losses |

*Thresholds are approximate and crop-dependent [@olsen1954;
@sharpley2003]. Consult local extension guidelines.*

### Interpretation of Bray-1 P

| Bray-1 P (mg/kg) | Classification | Agronomic Interpretation              |
|:------------------|:---------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Less than 10      | Very low       | P deficiency likely                   |
| 10 -- 20          | Low            | Fertilize to build P levels           |
| 20 -- 40          | Medium         | Adequate for most crops               |
| 40 -- 80          | High           | No additional P needed                |
| Greater than 80   | Very high      | Environmental risk                    |

### QC Requirements

- Prepare all standards in the same extractant matrix as the samples
  (matrix-matched calibration) to account for background color and
  ionic strength effects
- Run a reagent blank (extractant only, no soil) with each batch. The
  blank absorbance should be near zero at 880 nm.
- Run a laboratory reference soil with known extractable P in each
  batch. Recovery should be within +/- 15% of the established value.
- Run duplicate extractions on at least 10% of samples. Acceptable
  precision: relative percent difference (RPD) less than 15%.
- Calibration curve $r^2$ must be 0.995 or higher
- Check the mid-range standard after every 20 samples. Recalibrate if
  the check standard deviates by more than 10%.
- For Olsen extracts, verify the NaHCO~3~ pH is 8.5 +/- 0.1 before
  each batch; pH drift changes extraction efficiency substantially.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Olsen extracts (NaHCO~3~)    | Neutralize to pH 6--8 and drain, or collect for EH&S |
| Bray-1 extracts (NH~4~F/HCl) | Collect in fluoride waste carboy; EH&S pickup. Do not drain. |
| Color reagent waste (molybdate/H~2~SO~4~) | Collect in inorganic waste; EH&S pickup |
| Used filter paper and soil    | Standard trash (if non-hazardous soil)   |
| Spent charcoal                | Standard trash                           |

::: {.callout-warning}
### Fluoride Waste

Bray-1 extracts contain ammonium fluoride. **Do not pour down the
drain.** Collect all fluoride-containing waste in a labeled
polyethylene carboy for EH&S hazardous waste pickup.
:::

## Training Record

Before performing soil extractable P analyses independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for ammonium fluoride (if using Bray-1)
4. Demonstrate preparation of the extractant, color reagent, and
   calibration standards under supervision
5. Run a practice batch (at least 5 samples + blank + reference soil +
   duplicate) with acceptable QC results
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation in R {.appendix}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

# --- Calibration curve ---
standards <- tibble(
  P_mg_L = c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0),
  abs_880 = c(0.002, 0.018, 0.075, 0.148, 0.295, 0.740)
)

cal_model <- lm(abs_880 ~ P_mg_L, data = standards)
cat(sprintf("Calibration R-squared: %.5f\n", summary(cal_model)$r.squared))

# --- Sample calculation (Olsen method) ---
sample_abs <- 0.210            # Absorbance at 880 nm
soil_mass_g <- 2.50            # Air-dried soil (g)
extract_vol_mL <- 50           # Extractant volume (mL)
hygroscopic_moisture_pct <- 2.1 # Percent hygroscopic moisture

# Determine C from calibration
C_mg_L <- (sample_abs - coef(cal_model)[1]) / coef(cal_model)[2]

# Calculate soil extractable P (mg/kg dry soil)
P_soil_mg_kg <- C_mg_L * (extract_vol_mL / soil_mass_g) *
                ((100 + hygroscopic_moisture_pct) / 100)

cat(sprintf("Extract P concentration: %.3f mg/L\n", C_mg_L))
cat(sprintf("Olsen P:                %.1f mg/kg dry soil\n", P_soil_mg_kg))

# Interpret
interpret <- case_when(
  P_soil_mg_kg < 5  ~ "Very low",
  P_soil_mg_kg < 10 ~ "Low",
  P_soil_mg_kg < 20 ~ "Medium",
  P_soil_mg_kg < 40 ~ "High",
  TRUE               ~ "Very high"
)
cat(sprintf("Classification:         %s\n", interpret))
```
:::



## Appendix B: Reagent Preparation Quick Reference {.appendix}

### Olsen Extractant (0.5 M NaHCO~3~, pH 8.5)

1. Dissolve 42.0 g NaHCO~3~ in approximately 900 mL DI water
2. Adjust pH to 8.5 with 1 M NaOH (dropwise, with stirring)
3. Bring to 1 L with DI water
4. Check pH before each batch; re-adjust if needed
5. Prepare fresh weekly

### Bray-1 Extractant (0.03 M NH~4~F + 0.025 M HCl)

1. In a fume hood, dissolve 1.11 g NH~4~F in approximately 900 mL DI
   water
2. Add 2.1 mL concentrated HCl (12 M)
3. Bring to 1 L with DI water
4. Store in polyethylene at room temperature. Stable for several weeks.

### Combined Color Reagent (Murphy-Riley)

Mix in order, swirling between additions:

1. 50 mL of 5 N H~2~SO~4~
2. 15 mL of 4% ammonium molybdate
3. 5 mL of 0.274% antimony potassium tartrate
4. 30 mL of 1.76% ascorbic acid (freshly prepared)

Total volume: 100 mL. Prepare fresh for each analytical batch.

### P Stock Standard (1000 mg/L P)

1. Dry KH~2~PO~4~ at 105 C for 2 hours; cool in a desiccator
2. Dissolve 4.394 g in DI water in a 1 L volumetric flask
3. Bring to volume. Store at 4 C. Stable for months.

## Appendix D: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Yellow-brown Olsen extract    | Insufficient charcoal; charcoal not pre-washed | Increase charcoal; pre-wash with 0.5 M NaHCO~3~ |
| Calibration curve non-linear above 5 mg/L | Beer's Law limit exceeded | Dilute high samples; add lower standards |
| Bray-1 P unexpectedly low on calcareous soil | Acid neutralized by CaCO~3~ | Use Olsen method for soils with pH above 6.5 |
| Blank reads above 0.01 absorbance | Contaminated glassware or reagent | Acid-wash glassware ([SOP-L101](SOP-L101-glassware-cleaning.qmd)); prepare fresh reagents |
| Color fades after 30 min      | Ascorbic acid degradation       | Read within 30 min; prepare ascorbic acid solution fresh daily |
| Duplicates disagree by more than 15% RPD | Soil heterogeneity; inconsistent extraction timing | Homogenize soil more thoroughly; use a timer for extraction |
| Reference soil out of range   | Extractant pH drift (Olsen); reagent degradation | Verify NaHCO~3~ pH; remake color reagent |
